vulnerabilities.title: STACK_BUFFER_OVERFLOW_read_into_undersized_buffer

root_cause.description: In main, read(0, rbp-0x70, 0x100) reads up to 256 (0x100) bytes from stdin into a stack buffer located at rbp-0x70. The buffer is only 0x70 (112) bytes below the saved rbp. The stack frame is 0x80 bytes (sub rsp,0x80). The saved rbp resides at [rbp+0] and the return address at [rbp+8], which are at offsets 0x70 (112) and 0x78 (120) bytes from the buffer start respectively. Since read can write up to 256 bytes but the buffer only has 112 bytes of legitimate space before reaching saved rbp, the write overflows past the buffer boundary, overwrites the saved rbp (at offset 112) and the return address (at offset 120). There is no stack canary (F007) and no PIE (F001), so the overflow to the return address is neither detected nor randomized. The read return value is stored at [rbp-0x4] but is never used to bound or validate the amount written to the buffer — it is only used for newline stripping.

data_flow: Attacker sends up to 256 bytes via stdin
read(0, rbp-0x70, 0x100) at 0x401239 writes input into stack buffer at rbp-0x70
Buffer is 0x70=112 bytes below saved rbp; return address is at rbp+8 = offset 0x78=120 from buffer start
256-byte write exceeds 112-byte buffer space, overwriting saved rbp (offset 112) and return address (offset 120)
No canary check before leave;ret at 0x4012b9-0x4012ba
On loop exit (Y/y), leave;ret uses corrupted rbp and jumps to overwritten return address

security_check.expected: The size argument to read should not exceed the buffer capacity (0x70=112 bytes), or a stack canary should detect the overflow before function return.
security_check.actual: read is called with size 0x100 (256 bytes) into a buffer only 0x70 (112 bytes) from rbp. No stack canary is present. The read return value is stored but never used to validate or bound the write.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: Missing bounds check: read size (256) exceeds buffer capacity (112). Missing stack canary: no canary guards the saved rbp/return address. Missing return value validation: read() return value is not checked for errors or used to limit subsequent operations.

vulnerable_operation.target: stack buffer at rbp-0x70, overflowing into saved rbp [rbp+0] and return address [rbp+8]
vulnerable_operation.size: 256 bytes written into 112-byte buffer space (144 bytes of overflow past buffer end)

impact.reason: The overflow writes 144 bytes past the buffer boundary, corrupting the saved rbp and return address on the stack. With attacker-controlled input of 256 bytes, the return address at offset 120 from the buffer start is fully overwritable.
The saved rbp (stack frame pointer) at offset 112 and the return address at offset 120 are overwritten with attacker-controlled data, corrupting the function's control flow state.

evidence.description: Stack frame setup: add rsp,0xffffffffffffff80 (sub rsp,0x80) allocates 0x80=128 bytes of stack frame. Buffer at rbp-0x70 is 112 bytes below rbp.
lea rax,[rbp-0x70]; mov edx,0x100; mov rsi,rax; mov edi,0x0; call read@plt — read(0, rbp-0x70, 0x100) reads up to 256 bytes into buffer starting at rbp-0x70.

Buffer at rbp-0x70 (offset 0 from buffer start). Saved rbp at [rbp+0] = offset 0x70=112. Return address at [rbp+8] = offset 0x78=120. read writes up to 256 bytes, so offsets 112-255 are out-of-bounds, covering saved rbp (112) and return address (120).
leave; ret — function epilogue. leave restores rbp from corrupted [rbp+0], ret pops corrupted return address from [rbp+8]. No canary check precedes this.
read return value stored at [rbp-0x4] and reloaded, but only used for newline stripping (sub eax,0x1; cdqe; index into buffer). Never validated against buffer size or checked for read errors.

verification_required: Confirm exact offset from buffer start to return address is 120 bytes (0x78) by dynamic testing
Confirm no canary trap is triggered on overflow (static analysis shows none, but runtime confirmation needed)
Confirm the loop can be exited (Y/y input) after overflow to trigger the corrupted return

vulnerabilities.title: OOB_READ_read_return_value_signedness_mismatch

root_cause.description: After read(0, rbp-0x70, 0x100), the return value is stored as a 32-bit int at [rbp-0x4]. The code computes eax = return_value - 1, then uses cdqe to sign-extend the 32-bit result to 64 bits, and uses it as an index: movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rbp+rax*1-0x70]. If read returns 0 (EOF, e.g. closed stdin) or -1 (error), then eax-1 becomes -1 or -2 respectively. After cdqe sign-extension, rax becomes 0xffffffffffffffff or 0xfffffffffffffffe, causing [rbp+rax-0x70] to access memory far below the buffer (a large negative offset from rbp). This is an out-of-bounds read of 1 byte used only for comparison with 0x0a (newline check). The read return value is never checked for <= 0 before being used as an index.

attack_surface.input: stdin via read(0, rbp-0x70, 0x100) — specifically the EOF/error return path
data_flow: read() returns 0 (EOF) or -1 (error) when stdin is closed or error occurs
Return value stored at [rbp-0x4] as 32-bit int
movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rbp+rax*1-0x70] reads 1 byte at a large negative offset from rbp
Byte compared to 0x0a (newline); if match, another OOB write of NUL at same negative offset

security_check.expected: read() return value should be checked for <= 0 (error/EOF) before being used as a buffer index.
security_check.actual: Return value is used directly as (return_value - 1) index into the buffer without any check for error or EOF conditions.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: Missing return value validation: no check that read() returned a positive value before using (return_value - 1) as an array index.

vulnerable_operation.expression: movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rbp+rax*1-0x70] where rax = sign_extend(read_return_value - 1)
vulnerable_operation.target: stack memory at rbp + (negative index) - 0x70, i.e., below the buffer when read returns 0 or -1

impact.reason: When read returns 0 or -1, the sign-extended index causes a 1-byte read from memory far below the stack buffer. The read value is only used for comparison with 0x0a, limiting information exposure.

If the computed address [rbp+rax-0x70] with a huge negative rax falls in an unmapped page, the movzx load will cause SIGSEGV. This requires read() to return 0 or -1, which depends on stdin state (EOF or error).

evidence.description: mov [rbp-0x4],eax (store read return); mov eax,[rbp-0x4]; sub eax,0x1; cdqe; movzx eax,BYTE PTR [rbp+rax*1-0x70] — return value minus 1 is sign-extended and used as index without checking for <= 0.

cdqe at 0x401247 sign-extends eax to rax. If read returned 0, eax=-1, rax=0xffffffffffffffff, access at [rbp-0x70-1] = [rbp-0x71] (1 byte below buffer — minor). If read returned -1, eax=-2, rax=0xfffffffffffffffe, access at [rbp-0x70-2] = [rbp-0x72]. For typical small negative values the access is just below the buffer; the primary risk is using an unchecked return value as an index.

verification_required: Confirm whether read() can return 0 or -1 in the echo loop context (stdin EOF or error)
Confirm the actual memory effect of the negative index access — whether it crashes or reads adjacent stack data
Note: this is a secondary issue; the primary vulnerability is BUG-001 (stack buffer overflow)

non_vulnerabilities.reason: printf uses a fixed format string "%s" at 0x402025 with the user buffer as the data argument. The format string is not attacker-controlled, so this is not a format string vulnerability. The user buffer content is printed as-is. (Note: the buffer content is attacker-controlled due to BUG-001 overflow, but the printf call itself is not the vulnerability.)

scanf uses format "%7s" which limits input to 7 bytes, writing to rbp-0x78. The buffer at rbp-0x78 has adequate space (0x78 bytes to rbp, and the frame is 0x80 bytes). The %7s width specifier bounds the write. This is not a buffer overflow.

get_shell calls system with a fixed string "/bin/sh" at 0x402004. The argument is not attacker-controlled. get_shell is not called from main or any other function (F009). This is a win function at a fixed address (No PIE), relevant only as a potential target if the return address is corrupted via BUG-001, but the function itself has no vulnerability.
init disables buffering on standard streams and sets a 60-second alarm. All arguments are fixed constants. No attacker-controlled input reaches these calls. No vulnerability.

unresolved.description: ASLR status at runtime cannot be confirmed from static analysis
unresolved.reason: ASLR depends on kernel/runtime configuration. The binary is No-PIE so code/rodata addresses are fixed, but libc base would be ASLR-randomized if enabled. This affects exploit feasibility but not the vulnerability root cause.
unresolved.required_next_step: Runtime ASLR check by S3/S4 if libc-relative exploitation is attempted.

unresolved.reason: checksec did not report CET flags. If Shadow Stack (SHSTK) is enabled, the return address overwrite from BUG-001 would be detected at ret. This would reduce the impact of BUG-001 but does not eliminate the stack corruption.
unresolved.required_next_step: Runtime CET status check by S3/S4 to determine if return address overwrite is mitigated.
